title: Medical AI Needs Bedside Manners
gist: Paywalled teaser: Aurélie Jean and Sébastien Abgrall argue that even accurate medical AI has little value if it makes patients uneasy or burdens doctors, proposing a 'comfort-by-design' approach that involves patients and practitioners in development and fits existing medical practice.

insights.claim: Even the most accurate medical AI tools have little value if they make patients uneasy or doctors find them too cumbersome, making user comfort a key barrier to adoption.
insights.speaker: Aurélie Jean
insights.so_what: Clinical accuracy alone will not drive health-AI uptake; workflow fit and patient acceptance are adoption bottlenecks to watch.
insights.quote: Even the most accurate medical AI tools have little value if they make patients uneasy or doctors find them too cumbersome.

insights.claim: A 'comfort-by-design' approach, involving patients and practitioners in development and ensuring new systems work with existing medical practices, could overcome adoption obstacles for medical AI.
insights.speaker: Aurélie Jean
insights.so_what: Health-AI vendors that co-design with clinicians and integrate into existing workflows may win adoption faster.

insights.claim: AI tools in medicine are already helping patients take a more active role in managing their care and giving doctors access to information previously difficult or impossible to obtain.
insights.speaker: Aurélie Jean
insights.so_what: Health AI is already in use, so the adoption debate is shifting from capability to integration.
insights.locator: PARIS—AI is quickly finding its way
